sections.h2: LNG's share of alternative-fuel tonnage ordered rose to about 80% in 2026

chart.title: LNG took a larger share of alternative-fuel orders while the IMO rule stalled
chart.sub: Share of alternative-fuel tonnage ordered that chose LNG, %.

sections.means: Shipowners kept ordering LNG-fuelled tonnage while the IMO deliberated, because green methanol and ammonia still lack availability and bunkering.
sections.todo: Watch the resumed Second Extraordinary Session on 4 December 2026, which decides whether the Net-Zero Framework is adopted.

sections.h2: The dedicated LNG bunker-vessel fleet grew from 9 ships in 2017 to 67 today

chart.title: The LNG bunker-vessel fleet has grown from 9 vessels to 67
chart.source: Clarksons and other fleet trackers, as cited in the post.

sections.means: A refuelling network of 67 bunker vessels, with 42 more under construction through 2029, is what makes LNG the fuel ready today.
sections.todo: Track the 42 bunker vessels under construction through 2029 against the 60% growth forecast within three years.

sections.h2: Methane slip rises sharply at low engine load, eroding LNG's climate advantage

chart.title: Methane slip climbs from 2.3-3.0 to 21 g/kWh as engine load falls
chart.sub: Reported methane slip by engine load, g/kWh.
chart.source: Reported engine figures, as cited in the post.

sections.means: A ship idling or running slow burns dirtier on a lifecycle basis than the same ship at full power, so LNG's advantage can narrow or vanish.
sections.todo: Require slip control and load-aware reporting before LNG is counted as the cleaner choice, since methane enters the EU ETS from 2026.
